text:
anya: Heads-up — customer ran into runtime errors when importing our JS SDK in Cloudflare Workers (Pages). Error: "ReferenceError: crypto is not defined" and then a cascade because our auth helper pulls in node libs.

jay: Saw this too. Root cause: bundlers picking the wrong entrypoint and pulling in node-only transitive deps (process, Buffer). CF Workers doesn't provide those.

priya: Repro we used:

```js
addEventListener('fetch', e => {
  import('@redwood/inference').then(i => i.createClient({ apiKey: 'x' }).generate('hi'))
})
```

Throws because rollup/vite included a tiny process shim and fast-webcrypto in the bundle.

jay: Temporary mitigation: add a separate package entrypoint `./dist/esm-edge/index.mjs` and update package.json exports so bundlers prefer it for edge targets. Keep that build free of node shims.

anya: Also: AbortController was missing in one older runtime. We attached a guarded shim in our example app:

```
if (typeof globalThis.AbortController === 'undefined') {
  globalThis.AbortController = class { constructor(){ this.aborted=false; this.signal={aborted:false} } abort(){ this.aborted=true; this.signal.aborted=true }}
}
```

Works for basic streaming/retries but we must document limitations.

priya: TypeScript issue: public types reference NodeJS.Timer and `stream.Readable` in retry helpers. That breaks customers who compile with `lib: ['webworker']`. Plan: ship edge-specific .d.ts and point to it via exports -> types for the edge entry. Replace NodeJS.Timer uses with ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> or number to be portable.

jay: Auth rotation: remove `jsonwebtoken` from the edge build. Provide a fetch-based refresh helper that calls our token endpoint and returns the token, so customers don't need node jwt libs in the bundle.

anya: Docs + examples: add `examples/workers/minimal.mjs` showing recommended vite/esbuild flags and a miniflare snippet to run locally. Copy-pasteable is important for DX.

ci-bot: ci: queued workers-edge-smoke #7001

priya: Action items: jay -> create edge ESM target (tsup/rollup) that sets platform: 'browser' and externalizes node modules; anya -> example worker + miniflare test; priya -> split types and update docs. We'll keep shims opt-in and tiny, and avoid bundling heavy polyfills by default. :sparkles:
